scope: Targeted interdisciplinary review; separate from the 1990-record discovery catalog. Inclusion does not mean complete reading.

status_definitions.selected_sections: Selected original full-text passages consulted; no complete methods/supplement/reproduction audit.
status_definitions.abstract: Original author/publisher abstract consulted, including publisher-supplied Crossref or Europe PMC copies.
status_definitions.producer_documentation: Original data-producer documentation consulted; not a complete paper reading.
status_definitions.preview: Limited primary publisher/author indexed excerpts or book previews consulted.
status_definitions.prior_assessment: Earlier project assessment reconsulted; original source not freshly read beyond available preview this pass.
status_definitions.metadata: Bibliographic identification only; a reading lead, not scientific supporting evidence.

sources.title: The Borealis basin and the origin of the martian crustal dichotomy
sources.consulted: PubMed abstract.
sources.finding: Tharsis-compensated geometry supports a northern basin interpretation.
sources.limitation: Reconstruction and compensation assumptions matter; geometry is not a unique impact diagnosis.

sources.title: Investigating the feasibility of an impact-induced Martian Dichotomy
sources.consulted: Author arXiv abstract, https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.02466.
sources.finding: Impact feasibility depends on material strength and initial conditions.
sources.limitation: Simulation feasibility is not identification of the historical event.

sources.title: Combined impact and interior evolution models in three dimensions indicate a southern impact origin of the Martian Dichotomy
sources.consulted: Existing project abstract assessment and current indexed author preview; author PDF could not be opened.
sources.finding: Impact and subsequent interior evolution are modelled together.
sources.limitation: Full methods and parameter coverage were not reassessed; conditional southern-impact preference.

sources.title: A Positive Feedback Between Crustal Thickness and Melt Extraction for the Origin of the Martian Dichotomy
sources.consulted: Earlier project source notes; full-text access blocked in this pass.
sources.finding: Asymmetric crust growth can be amplified through thermal/melt feedback.
sources.limitation: An amplification mechanism does not automatically establish its initial trigger or degree-one selection.

sources.title: Martian Highlands Differentiation Concomitant to Dichotomy Formation
sources.consulted: DLR author PDF: abstract and introductory/model-context passages.
sources.finding: Parameterized evolution links dichotomy growth and highland differentiation.
sources.limitation: A simplified mantle/lithosphere framework is not a regional reconstruction.

sources.title: InSight Constraints on the Global Character of the Martian Crust
sources.consulted: Publisher-supplied Crossref abstract.
sources.finding: Local seismic information constrains global crustal models.
sources.limitation: Global thickness remains conditional on density, composition and modelling assumptions.

sources.title: Global Crustal Thickness Revealed by Surface Waves Orbiting Mars
sources.consulted: Publisher-supplied Crossref abstract.
sources.finding: Orbiting surface waves constrain path-averaged crustal structure.
sources.limitation: Sparse paths and adopted structure do not constitute uniform global seismic sampling.

sources.title: Crustal Density Differences Along Mars' Dichotomy Boundary From Gravity and Topography
sources.consulted: NASA product description, model variants and uncertainty description: https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/102.
sources.finding: Boundary-constrained gravity analysis supplies alternative density estimates and ensembles.
sources.limitation: Paper methods not fully audited; estimates and covariance-derived clones form one inference family.

sources.title: Seismic evidence for a melt-depleted lower crust and transcrustal magmatism on Mars
sources.consulted: Publisher main text and selected modelling passages.
sources.finding: Petrological interpretation links local deeper crust to melt-depleted cumulates.
sources.limitation: Local InSight inference and assumed mineral equilibria do not establish a global layer.

sources.title: Composition of the Martian Crust and Its Relationship to the Martian Mantle: A Post‐InSight View
sources.consulted: Publisher abstract and availability statement.
sources.finding: Review connects post-InSight crustal composition and mantle inventories.
sources.limitation: Synthesis estimates are not additional independent observations.

sources.title: Tidal tomography reveals a thermal anomaly beneath Mars’s crustal dichotomy
sources.consulted: Publisher abstract, thermal interpretation and selected methods passages.
sources.finding: Tidal interpretation indicates a present southern thermal anomaly.
sources.limitation: Temperature conversion depends on rheology and corrections; origin and ancient temperature remain indirect.

sources.title: Constraints on the Origin of the Martian Dichotomy From Southern Highlands Marsquakes
sources.consulted: Publisher indexed passages and earlier project notes.
sources.finding: Southern marsquakes add regional attenuation evidence.
sources.limitation: Source, scattering and geometry complicate thermal and origin interpretations; date conventions differ.

sources.title: Geophysical evidence for an enriched molten silicate layer above Mars’s core
sources.consulted: Prior project abstract assessment reconsulted; no complete current methods reading.
sources.finding: A molten silicate layer changes interpretation of core structure.
sources.limitation: Present structure does not independently date the dynamo or establish its past power source.

sources.title: Seismic detection of a 600-km solid inner core in Mars
sources.consulted: Publisher abstract, main interpretation and selected phase-identification methods.
sources.finding: Seismic phases are interpreted as a present solid inner core.
sources.limitation: Inference depends on phase assignment and structure; associated correction must accompany reuse.

sources.title: Author Correction: Seismic detection of a 600-km solid inner core in Mars
sources.consulted: Correction linked on main article; earlier project correction note reconsulted. Current full notice could not be reopened.
sources.finding: Correction notice associated with the inner-core paper.
sources.limitation: Not an independent result; details must be rechecked before numerical reproduction.

sources.title: Experimental constraints on a long-lived magma layer at the Martian core–mantle boundary
sources.consulted: Publisher indexed abstract/material-physics excerpts; direct full page unavailable.
sources.finding: Experiments constrain the physical viability of dense basal melts.
sources.limitation: A laboratory constraint is not a direct Martian boundary-layer detection; full methods outstanding.
sources.metadata_provenance: Primary publisher, author repository or original abstract metadata

sources.title: A New Model of the Crustal Magnetic Field of Mars Using MGS and MAVEN
sources.consulted: Catalog abstract and existing project magnetic-model notes reconsulted.
sources.finding: MGS and MAVEN measurements support a crustal field model.
sources.limitation: A field map is not a unique source-magnetization or paleointensity map.

sources.title: Depth of Martian Magnetization From Localized Power Spectrum Analysis
sources.consulted: Publisher-supplied Crossref abstract.
sources.finding: Localized magnetic spectra constrain equivalent source depths.
sources.limitation: Thin-source and spectral assumptions do not give unique physical layer boundaries.

sources.title: Timing of the martian dynamo: New constraints for a core field 4.5 and 3.7 Ga ago
sources.consulted: Existing project abstract/source notes reconsulted.
sources.finding: Selected geological units imply possible early and later dynamo activity.
sources.limitation: Orbital sources inherit uncertain geological age association.

sources.title: Paleomagnetic evidence for a long-lived, potentially reversing martian dynamo at ~3.9 Ga
sources.consulted: Author abstract, https://dash.harvard.edu/entities/publication/68f0ab8f-d50d-4cd5-bdaa-81e9052b9dca.
sources.finding: ALH 84001 components support an ancient, potentially reversing field interpretation.
sources.limitation: Acquisition chronology and coordinate reconstruction remain necessary.

sources.title: Weak magnetism of Martian impact basins may reflect cooling in a reversing dynamo
sources.consulted: Publisher indexed abstract; complete page could not be opened this pass.
sources.finding: Reversing fields during cooling can reduce basin-scale magnetic signals.
sources.limitation: Tested basin sizes and carrier/cooling assumptions limit extrapolation.

sources.title: Magnetic Properties of Martian Impact Basins Including the Effect of Mantle Excavation
sources.consulted: Author publication list: https://jmdday.scrippsprofiles.ucsd.edu/publications/.
sources.finding: Lead for assessing mantle excavation and basin magnetic properties.
sources.limitation: Primary scientific text not assessed here; not used as supporting result.
sources.metadata_provenance: Primary publisher, author repository or original abstract metadata

sources.title: Mars' Hemispheric Magnetic Field From a Full‐Sphere Dynamo
sources.consulted: Publisher abstract and indexed introductory/discussion sections.
sources.finding: Nonuniform core-boundary heat flux can produce asymmetric full-sphere dynamos.
sources.limitation: Imposed boundary conditions and temporal averaging must match rock recording.

sources.title: Hand Magnets and the Destruction of Ancient Meteorite Magnetism
sources.consulted: Publisher abstract; earlier project selected-section notes retained separately.
sources.finding: Handling overprints compromise the tested meteorites magnetic archives.
sources.limitation: The investigated stones do not represent every untested paired stone or invalidate their geochemistry.

sources.title: Paleointensity and Rock Magnetism of Martian Nakhlite Meteorite Miller Range 03346: Evidence for Intense Small‐Scale Crustal Magnetization on Mars
sources.consulted: Existing project selected-section assessment reconsulted.
sources.finding: MIL 03346 permits a local crustal-field interpretation of a young record.
sources.limitation: A young recorded field need not be a core dynamo; no new intensity extracted here.

sources.title: Opaque minerals, magnetic properties, and paleomagnetism of the Tissint Martian meteorite
sources.consulted: Existing project mineralogical and magnetic source notes reconsulted.
sources.finding: Tissint links carrier properties and remanence interpretations.
sources.limitation: Crystallization age cannot substitute automatically for acquisition age.

sources.title: Likely Ferromagnetic Minerals Identified by the Perseverance Rover and Implications for Future Paleomagnetic Analyses of Returned Martian Samples
sources.consulted: Publisher indexed abstract and introductory passages.
sources.finding: Perseverance observations identify promising magnetic-mineral candidates.
sources.limitation: Carrier identification does not supply returned-sample laboratory paleointensity.

sources.title: Ground magnetic survey on Mars from the Zhurong rover
sources.consulted: Catalog abstract and existing regional source notes reconsulted.
sources.finding: Zhurong measures a weak local northern surface field.
sources.limitation: One traverse cannot characterize all northern crustal magnetization.

sources.title: Evidence for extremely rapid magma ocean crystallization and crust formation on Mars
sources.consulted: Original article abstract served through Europe PMC.
sources.finding: Ancient zircon dates and Hf modelling constrain early crustal production.
sources.limitation: Mineral ages and source model ages are different constraints; neither dates the dichotomy directly.

sources.title: A tale of two planets: Disparate evolutionary models for Mars inferred from radiogenic isotope compositions of Martian meteorites
sources.consulted: Original article abstract served through Europe PMC; PMC full page blocked.
sources.finding: Different meteorite groups imply different reservoir histories.
sources.limitation: Meteorite-source histories do not uniquely map onto hemispheres.
sources.metadata_provenance: Primary publisher, author repository or original abstract metadata

sources.title: Zircon trace element evidence for early hydrothermal activity on Mars
sources.consulted: Europe PMC abstract plus accessible indexed original discussion passages.
sources.finding: Zircon chemistry and inclusions support an early hydrothermal interpretation.
sources.limitation: The studied grain does not yield a measured ancient paleofield or global water inventory.

sources.title: Dating recent aqueous activity on Mars
sources.consulted: Publisher methods, results and diffusion/resetting discussion: https://www.geochemicalperspectivesletters.org/article2443/.
sources.finding: Micro-encapsulated Ar-Ar analyses date Lafayette iddingsite.
sources.limitation: Alteration dating is local and is not magnetic acquisition dating; diffusion assumptions matter.

sources.title: Gravity and Magnetic Field Signatures in Hydrothermally Affected Regions on Mars
sources.consulted: DLR article PDF, abstract and joint-inversion method, especially section 3.2.1.
sources.finding: Joint gravity/magnetic structures are interpreted in hydrothermal contexts.
sources.limitation: Structural coupling is imposed as regularization; association is not independent proof of alteration.

sources.title: A Mars orbital catalog of aqueous alteration signatures (MOCAAS)
sources.consulted: Earlier project abstract and data-policy assessment reconsulted.
sources.finding: Orbital mineral detections map exposed aqueous alteration signatures.
sources.limitation: Nondetection depends on coverage and exposure; no new raw data redistributed.

sources.title: Long-term drying of Mars by sequestration of ocean-scale volumes of water in the crust
sources.consulted: Original article abstract served through Europe PMC.
sources.finding: Crustal sequestration can contribute substantially in water-evolution models.
sources.limitation: Fractions depend on assumed reservoirs and fluxes; not a direct measured global partition.
sources.metadata_provenance: Primary publisher, author repository or original abstract metadata

sources.title: Liquid water in the Martian mid-crust
sources.consulted: Author-repository indexed abstract and result excerpts.
sources.finding: Rock-physics interpretation favours water-filled fractured mid-crust beneath InSight.
sources.limitation: Alternative material models and global extrapolation remain separate questions.
sources.metadata_provenance: Primary publisher, author repository or original abstract metadata

sources.title: Direct Detection of Hydrogen Reveals a New Macroscopic Crustal Water Reservoir on Early Mars
sources.consulted: Publisher indexed abstract; article published 13 August 2026.
sources.finding: Combined imaging identifies hydrogen-bearing material in NWA 7034.
sources.limitation: Full origin/weathering controls and scaling to global inventory require methods audit.
sources.metadata_provenance: Primary publisher, author repository or original abstract metadata

sources.title: Fundamental constraints and questions from the study of Martian meteorites and the need for returned samples
sources.consulted: Publisher-supplied Crossref abstract.
sources.finding: Meteorite review identifies sampling gaps and returned-sample needs.
sources.limitation: Coverage statements refer to the sample set assessed at publication, not all later finds.

sources.title: First direct observations of atmospheric sputtering at Mars
sources.consulted: Original article abstract served through Europe PMC.
sources.finding: MAVEN observations identify present atmospheric sputtering.
sources.limitation: Present escape observations are not a directly measured ancient integrated loss.
sources.metadata_provenance: Primary publisher, author repository or original abstract metadata

sources.title: Why an intrinsic magnetic field does not protect a planet against atmospheric escape
sources.consulted: Publisher indexed abstract and discussion excerpts.
sources.finding: Escape pathways respond differently to intrinsic magnetization in idealized comparisons.
sources.limitation: Neither universal shielding nor universal enhancement follows for every atmosphere and epoch.
sources.metadata_provenance: Primary publisher, author repository or original abstract metadata

sources.title: A coupled model of episodic warming, oxidation and geochemical transitions on early Mars
sources.consulted: Publisher abstract.
sources.finding: Coupled atmospheric/geochemical modelling explores episodic warming and oxidation.
sources.limitation: A conditional climate history is not a measured global sequence.

sources.title: Episodic warm climates on early Mars primed by crustal hydration
sources.consulted: Author abstract and indexed model passages; author repository and Caltech manuscript located.
sources.finding: Hydration-associated chemistry can supply hydrogen for episodic warm climates in a model.
sources.limitation: Net fluid/reactant budgets and atmospheric assumptions must be carried into any joint model.

sources.title: Dichotomy retreat and aqueous alteration on Noachian Mars recorded in highland remnants
sources.consulted: Publisher abstract and indexed methods excerpts.
sources.finding: Highland remnants near Mawrth preserve evidence of alteration and margin retreat.
sources.limitation: Regional remnant mapping does not reconstruct the entire primordial boundary.

sources.title: Gravity-driven fold-thrust belt at the Martian dichotomy
sources.consulted: Publisher indexed preview and existing project abstract notes.
sources.finding: Nilosyrtis structures motivate gravity-driven extension and shortening.
sources.limitation: Mapped kinematics cannot be replaced by a simple topographic flexure fit.

sources.title: Late Tharsis formation and implications for early Mars
sources.consulted: Publisher abstract.
sources.finding: Tharsis timing and reorientation affect reconstructed paleogeography.
sources.limitation: Reference-frame choices do not independently establish every event age or climate history.

sources.title: Ancient ocean coastal deposits imaged on Mars
sources.consulted: Author PDF: abstract and early results/discussion pages.
sources.finding: Buried dipping radar reflectors are interpreted as coastal deposits along the traverse.
sources.limitation: Local sedimentary interpretation and regional age context do not identify a synchronous global shoreline.

sources.title: Accretion of Phobos and Deimos in an extended debris disc stirred by transient moons
sources.consulted: Publisher abstract preview.
sources.finding: An impact debris disc with transient moons can form small satellites in simulations.
sources.limitation: Does not prove the satellite-forming event was the dichotomy-forming impact.
sources.metadata_provenance: Primary publisher, author repository or original abstract metadata

sources.title: Origin of Phobos and Deimos by the impact of a Vesta-to-Ceres sized body with Mars
sources.consulted: Indexed original PMC abstract and model excerpts.
sources.finding: Impact-disc evolution offers another satellite-formation parameter range.
sources.limitation: A feasible disc model does not uniquely determine Mars impact history.

sources.title: Planetary Crusts: Their Composition, Origin and Evolution

sources.title: Mars: An Introduction to its Interior, Surface and Atmosphere
sources.consulted: Cambridge chapter summaries/preview.
